title: Microsoft Forms: Copilot in Forms for US Government clouds
summary: Hold: the statement that government-cloud prerequisites are not documented is too broad. Microsoft publishes qualifying prerequisite licences for its government-cloud Copilot add-on; the roadmap facts and the briefing's account of conflicting drafting entitlements are supported.

claims.claim: Forms is a tool for collecting survey responses, including organisational and customer feedback.
claims.quote: In business organizations, it can be used to collect customer feedback, measure employee satisfaction, improve your product or business, or organize company events.

claims.claim: Copilot drafts forms from what a user types.
claims.quote: Authors can simply type a prompt using natural language, and watch Copilot generate a form draft to get started.

claims.claim: Copilot can use user-referenced material to draft a form.
claims.quote: When creating a form with Copilot, users can now reference existing documents such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Users can also reference an existing form by pasting the form's URL into the prompt box.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot's results analysis uses the responses collected by the form.
claims.quote: The Copilot chat pane is now built into Microsoft Forms, helping users improve forms and quizzes, draft and send invitations, and analyze responses.

claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available in GCC, GCC High, and DoD, and operates entirely within the customer's U.S. government cloud tenant.

claims.claim: Any government-cloud-specific prerequisites are not yet documented.

Microsoft publishes eligible prerequisite licences in the US Government section of https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options. Keep the separate, narrower statement that the government-cloud feature-by-feature licence split is not specified.
